focus: /θ/ (three, thirty) vs /t/ and /s/ · -TEEN vs -ty stress · final clusters (six, twelfth) · /v/ vs /f/ (five, four) · days of the week /deɪ/
focus_ar: صوت /θ/ مقابل /t/ و /s/، والفرق في النبر بين -teen و -ty، والتجمعات الساكنة في النهاية، و /v/ مقابل /f/، وأيام الأسبوع
arabic_challenge: Arabic has ث (/θ/) but learners often substitute /t/ or /s/ in English (three → tree/sree). Arabic has no /v/, so 'five' becomes 'fife'. The -teen/-ty stress difference decides whether you say 13 or 30 — a real-world money and time problem.

isolation.instructions: /θ/ = tongue tip between the teeth, NO voice, air flows continuously (like Arabic ث). /t/ stops the air completely. /s/ keeps the tongue behind the teeth with a sharp hiss.
isolation.instructions_ar: /θ/ طرف اللسان بين الأسنان، بدون صوت، والهوا مستمر (زي ث). /t/ يوقف الهوا. /s/ اللسان خلف الأسنان وصفير حاد.

sentence_practice: My birthday is the third of the month.
daily_drills.record_this: Three plus three is six. My birthday is on the third of this month, and I have thirty-three books.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'three'. If you can't see your tongue in a mirror, you are probably saying 'tree'.

isolation.instructions: 13-19 end in -TEEN with stress on the LAST syllable: thir-TEEN. 30-90 end in -ty with stress on the FIRST syllable and a short, weak ending: THIR-ty. Getting this wrong changes the number.
isolation.instructions_ar: الأرقام 13-19 النبر على الآخر: thir-TEEN. والأرقام 30-90 النبر على الأول والنهاية خفيفة: THIR-ty. الخطأ هنا يغيّر الرقم.

sentence_practice: It costs FIFty pounds, not fifTEEN.
There are SIXty minutes in an hour.
daily_drills.record_this: I am thirteen years old, not thirty. It costs fifty pounds, not fifteen. There are sixty minutes in one hour.
daily_drills.self_check: Ask a friend to write the number they hear. Did they write 13 or 30 — the one you meant?

isolation.instructions: English lets consonants pile up at the end: six /ks/, seven /vn/, twelfth /lfθ/, first /rst/, months /nθs/. Arabic usually breaks these up with a vowel — resist that. Say the consonants together, quickly and lightly.
isolation.instructions_ar: الإنجليزي بيجمع سواكن في آخر الكلمة: six، twelfth، first، months. العربي بيفصلها بحركة — قاوم ده ونطقها ورا بعض بسرعة وخِفّة.

daily_drills.record_this: Six weeks and seven months. My exam is on the first, and the next one is on the twelfth.
daily_drills.self_check: Count the syllables in 'months'. It must be ONE, not two.

isolation.instructions: Both use the top teeth on the bottom lip. /f/ has NO voice (just air). /v/ has VOICE — the throat buzzes. Arabic has no /v/, so 'five' often becomes 'fife'.
isolation.instructions_ar: الاتنين الأسنان العليا على الشفة السفلى. /f/ بدون صوت. /v/ بصوت — الحلق يهتز. العربي مفيهاش /v/ فـ 'five' تبقى 'fife'.
practice: vvv (hand on throat — feel the buzz)

daily_drills.record_this: Five, seven, eleven and twelve. I have seven books, not four. Every November has thirty days.
daily_drills.self_check: Put a hand on your throat and say 'five'. You must feel a buzz at the END of the word.

isolation.instructions: Days are stressed on the FIRST syllable: MON-day, TUES-day. In natural speech the '-day' ending is often weak (/di/), not a strong 'DAY'. Say MON-di, not mon-DAY.
isolation.instructions_ar: أيام الأسبوع النبر على المقطع الأول: MON-day. وفي الكلام الطبيعي نهاية -day تبقى خفيفة، مش مضغوطة.
practice: clap on the FIRST syllable only

sentence_practice: Today is Monday and tomorrow is Tuesday.
I work from Sunday to Thursday.
On Friday and Saturday I rest.
daily_drills.record_this: Today is Monday and tomorrow is Tuesday. I work from Sunday to Thursday, and on Friday and Saturday I rest at home.
daily_drills.self_check: Note that 'Wednesday' has only THREE syllables (WED-nes-day) — the first 'd' is silent.

challenge_sentences: Three, thirteen, thirty — say each one clearly.
My birthday is the fourth of this month.
daily_drills.record_this: Three, thirteen and thirty. Five plus seven is twelve. My birthday is the fourth of this month. Today is Thursday the twelfth, and I have thirty-five books.
daily_drills.self_check: Have someone write down every number they hear. Do their numbers match yours exactly?

test_yourself.instructions: Record yourself reading this aloud. Then listen back and check each sound group.
test_yourself.instructions_ar: سجّل نفسك وانت تقرأ ده بصوت عالي، وبعدين اسمع وراجع كل مجموعة أصوات.
test_yourself.passage: Today is Thursday, the third of the month. I get up at seven and I finish work at five. There are sixty minutes in an hour and twenty-four hours in a day. I am thirteen years old — not thirty! Next month I will be fourteen. My class has fifteen students, and the school has fifty teachers. Five plus seven is twelve.

sounds_to_check./θ/ (not /t/ or /s/): Thursday, third, month, thirteen, thirty, three
sounds_to_check.-TEEN vs -ty: thirTEEN vs THIRty, fourTEEN vs FORty, fifTEEN vs FIFty, SIXty, TWENty
sounds_to_check.final clusters: months, first, next, six, twelfth, asked
sounds_to_check./v/ vs /f/: five, seven, twelve, eleven — four, fourteen, fifty, finish

scoring_guide.90_100: Numbers are unambiguous and every /θ/ is dental. Ready for week 4.
scoring_guide.70_89: Clear overall; occasional /v/ → /f/ or a rushed cluster.
scoring_guide.50_69: 13/30 confusion persists, or 'three' sounds like 'tree'. Repeat days 1-2.
scoring_guide.below_50: Redo days 1-4, focusing on the mirror check and the throat-buzz check.

for_arabic_speakers: You already have ث — use it. 'Three' needs the tongue visible between the teeth.
/v/ does not exist in Arabic. Practise the throat buzz: fff (silent) → vvv (buzzing).
The -teen/-ty stress difference is a real-life risk with prices, ages and times. Over-emphasise it at first.
Never insert a vowel to break up a final cluster: 'six', not 'si-kis'.
supplementary_notes.recording_requirement: Record the 'record_this' line daily; on day 7 compare against day 1.
